# R4 — Justification

Every semantic unit of `artifact/library/core/rules/R4-commit-is-not-publish.md`,
why it exists, what breaks if it is removed, and where the idea comes from.

| # | Unit | Why it exists | What breaks if removed | Source / inspiration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Opening: private, and public only through "an action that sends it somewhere you cannot recall" | One test covers every case the list misses: reversibility. | The rule becomes a closed list to argue around — anything unnamed is "not publishing". | Blueprint non-negotiable "Commit is not publish"; cargo's permanence model (`SOURCES.md` #5) |
| 2 | `## Private` + the five local acts (commit, tag, build, installer, archive) | Names the things an agent already does and might pause over, so ordinary work is not gated. | Either the agent asks permission to commit (wasting a question) or it stops after building. | bevy `_release-content` (drafts live in the repo); MonoGame `build` job |
| 3 | "Do them inside the approved task without asking again." | The task approval already covered local work; asking again spends an R2 question on a non-question. | The 3-per-stage budget is consumed by "may I commit?", and real choices go unasked. | R2; blueprint metric "questions that changed a decision ≥ 50%" |
| 4 | `## Publish actions` + "an explicit user command naming the action and the target" | Defines the shape of permission, so "ok" or "ship it" cannot be stretched into a push to anywhere. | Vague assent becomes a blanket licence; nobody can say what was authorised. | Mindustry `on: push: tags: v*`; MonoGame `if: github.ref_type == 'tag'` |
| 5 | Push bullet, "including a pushed tag", plus the line in `## Private`: a local tag is private, pushing it publishes | The most common accidental publish: pushing a tag *is* cutting a release once CI listens for tags. | A reader concludes a local tag is both private and a publish and takes whichever half suits the moment; `git push --tags` ships from a session that only meant to back up. | MonoGame release step gated on a tag ref; Mindustry tag trigger |
| 6 | Deploy / store upload bullet | The irreversible end of the pipeline; a store upload starts review and may go live on its own. | "Deploy" is read as the last step of finishing a task rather than a separate decision. | libgdx `staging-deploy` -> jreleaser Central; gh `--draft` |
| 7 | Paid spend bullet | Money is the only category with no rollback at all, and the agent can reach it alone. | The agent buys an asset or a service tier to unblock itself, and the user learns from an invoice. | Blueprint R4 ("or spend"); R2 irreversible / missing-data |
| 8 | Public post bullet | A post publishes the *game*, not the code — a different risk surface that a code-centric rule would miss. | The agent announces a release that does not exist yet, or leaks a date. | bevy "will be published to the website during the next release" (draft ≠ published) |
| 9 | Sending a build or link to anyone, testers included | "Sharing" reads as a favour and is the quietest way for a private build to travel. | A private build circulates; an embargo or store plan breaks with no trace. | MonoGame uploading artifacts on every push (rejected, `SOURCES.md` #1) |
| 10 | "I will just publish it is not a command. Silence is not a yes." | Names the two phrasings an agent uses to authorise itself, in the words it actually uses. | Intent is treated as permission and no record shows who allowed it. | `template/opencode.json` (permission is a config fact, not a mood) |
| 11 | `## Before` + diff or artifact with size | The user must see what leaves the machine; size is a cheap fingerprint of the exact file. | A publish happens on a build nobody inspected. | R1 evidence; MonoGame artifact-staging steps |
| 12 | Target: remote and branch, store and channel, person | "Push" and "upload" are ambiguous; the target is the part that is wrong when it goes wrong. | A correct build lands on the wrong channel, account, or person. | gh `--verify-tag`; libgdx named staging repository |
| 13 | The version | Versions are what stores, changelogs, and rollback refer to; without one a publish cannot be recalled precisely. | Two artifacts claim one version and rollback restores the wrong one. | Mindustry `RELEASE_VERSION` derived from the tag |
| 14 | Rollback path, including whether an unpublish step exists | Forces the honest answer that many publishes have no undo, before the decision rather than after. | The agent promises a rollback that does not exist and the user relies on it. | cargo permanence; gh `--draft` as the pre-publish escape |
| 15 | "Dry-run where the tool offers it." | A free rehearsal catches a wrong target or credential while it is still harmless. | The first real publish is also the first test of the command. | goreleaser `--snapshot`; `cargo publish --dry-run` (`SOURCES.md` #5, #6) |
| 16 | "Then wait for a clear yes." | Makes the gate a wait; a summary followed by immediate action is a notification, not consent. | The agent shows the summary and publishes in the same turn, so the message never had a chance to stop it. | Blueprint non-goal "Auto-publish"; MonoGame tag gate |
| 17 | "Commit and push are separate commands. Never chain them." | Chaining is the mechanical cause of the accident: one line merges the private and public categories the rule separates. | The rule is honoured in intent and violated by a single `&&`. | `template/opencode.json` (allow `git status`, deny `git push`) |
| 18 | `## Never`: no auto-push, no auto-tag, no auto-release | Closes the class "helpful automation", which is how publishing gets added back a week later. | A release workflow is added "for convenience" and now publishes on merge. | semantic-release, the rejected model (`SOURCES.md` "Considered") |
| 19 | "Never publish from an autonomous run: stop and report what is staged for release." | Autonomy removes the person who would say yes; the run must have a legal way to end blocked. | An overnight run ships to a store and the report arrives after the fact. | Blueprint autonomy section ("commit is not publish"); R2 hard-stop list |
| 20 | `## Secrets` paragraph | Publishing is exactly where keys are used, so the leak surface belongs in this rule. | The agent puts a token in a URL or pastes it in chat to make the push work. | MonoGame scoping `NUGET_API_KEY` to the deploy job; X02 |
| 21 | "If one appears in output, stop and report an incident." | A leaked key needs rotation, not a warning; it is a different action from "be careful". | The agent continues, pastes the value again, and the leak widens. | Mindustry PATs embedded in push URLs (rejected) |
| 22 | `## Remote` + `git remote -v` and `git branch --show-current` | Two cheap commands catch the real failure: the right publish to the wrong repository or branch. | A release is cut from a fork or a scratch branch. | MonoGame tag-ref gate; gh `--verify-tag` |
| 23 | `## After`: release evidence per R1, read by G3 | Attaches the publish to the existing evidence system and the existing gate instead of inventing a second log. | Publishes leave no trace and G3 has nothing to judge. | R1 release row; blueprint G3 |
| 24 | `## Enforcement`: the deny list in the project `opencode.json` (shipped in this template as `template/opencode.json`), user runs it or grants per command, never widened | Turns the rule from advice into default-deny config, and names the file at the path a game repo actually has, so the line survives the copy out of the template. | In a game repo the rule points at a `template/` directory that is not there, and the deny list becomes unfindable. | `template/opencode.json` (`git push *`, `gh release create *` denied); blueprint "Permissions are law; rules are advice" |
| 25 | `## Unavailable`: stop, report what is ready, the command, the target; nothing ships | Gives the agent a legal exit that is not "publish and explain later". | Pressure to finish the task converts into a publish. | R2 `BLOCKING —` pattern; R1 "when it cannot run" |
| 26 | Boundary line: R1 evidence, R2 questions, E12 scores | Prevents three parts from restating one idea and names the scorer. | Duplication and drift: two rules disagree and the agent follows the last one read. | Blueprint "one fact in one place"; rubric §1 |

## Deliberate omissions

| Omitted | Reason |
|---|---|
| Per-store upload steps and channel names | P01 owns stores; core must not name a platform, and the list would rot faster than it helps. |
| Version numbering and tag naming | X03 owns semver and `agent.lock.json`; one rule already covers `VERSION`. |
| The permission file's schema and syntax | X02 and the skeleton own it; `template/opencode.json` is the fact, and copying it here would drift. |
| A verbatim script for "a clear yes" | It would become a phrase the user must match; the rule asks for consent, not a password. |
| Platform-specific unpublish rules (review windows, delisting) | P01 owns them; core would be wrong for most stores on the day it was written. |
| A second list of secret types | X02 owns secrets; two lists diverge and the shorter one wins by being easier to read. |
| Legal and licensing review of a public post | P07 and X02 own it; R4 only says the post is a publish action. |
